chunks.text: Hi — I'm a solo Chinese builder, based in San Francisco,
and this is sotto.
Before sotto, a hackathon project of mine grew into web3 games
that reached up to two million mainnet transactions a month.
So I know what it takes to turn a hackathon build into something people use every day.
Now I'm building payments for AI agents.
Agents are starting to buy their own data and APIs,
and today every one of those payments is public:
what they bought, from whom, and for how much.
And nothing caps what an agent can spend.
sotto makes those payments confidential by default,
limited by a policy the owner sets,
and auditable with viewing keys.
The public sees that a payment happened, not what it was.
The owner sees every receipt, and an auditor can check exact amounts from the chain.
It works with what agents already use:
x402, the Machine Payments Protocol, an MCP server and an Agent Skill.
chunks.say: x-four-oh-two, the Machine Payments Protocol, an M C P server, and an Agent Skill.

chunks.text: And it runs end to end on Solana, Tempo and Zcash —
chunks.say: And it runs end to end on Solana, Tempo, and Zee-cash —

chunks.text: where it's already live on the new NU7 testnet upgrade.
chunks.say: where it's already live on the new N U seven testnet upgrade.

chunks.text: Why me?
I've already taken a hackathon project to millions of mainnet transactions, and I ship fast.
Working solo with Anthropic's Claude Code, I built sotto in three weeks:
chunks.say: Working solo with Anthropic's Clawed Code, I built sotto in three weeks:

chunks.text: the SDK, the MCP server, and a Rust Zcash service.
chunks.say: the S.D.K., the M.C.P. server, and a Rust Zee-cash service.

chunks.text: Why now?
Solana's confidential transfers came back to mainnet this June,
and almost nobody uses them yet.
Agents are just starting to pay for things.
The rails are ready, and nobody has laid them for agents.
I'm looking for the accelerator, and a first design partner whose agents buy data.
sotto: confidential, not anonymous. Thank you.
chunks.say: Sotto. Confidential, not anonymous. Thank you.
